paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
caption_used: Massive activation values across layers under baseline conditions, showing four component signals. The ffn_residual (red solid) and attn_residual (orange dotted) lines rise sharply at layer 5 to approximately 1400, with ffn_residual maintaining values between 1400 and 1600 through layer 20 before declining. The attn_residual closely mirrors ffn_residual but with a one-layer rightward shift. The ffn_output (green dash-dot) exhibits periodic spikes at layers 5, 13, and 22, reaching peak values of approximately 800. The attn_output (blue dashed) remains near zero throughout all layers, with no notable increase at any point in the network. The data indicates that massive activations in the baseline are driven primarily by the feed-forward network residual stream, with attention outputs contributing negligibly.

model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The diagram illustrates the maximum activation values across layers for four distinct signal components under baseline conditions. The horizontal axis, labeled “Layer,” represents layer indices from 0 to 20, with uniform integer tick marks at intervals of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20). The vertical axis, labeled “Max Activation Value,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1600, with tick marks at intervals of 200 (0, 200, 400, 600, 800, 1000, 1200, 1400, 1600).

The “attn_output” signal (blue dashed line) remains near zero throughout all layers, with values consistently below 100 across the entire range from layer 0 to layer 20.

The “attn_residual” signal (orange dotted line) rises sharply at layer 5 to approximately 1400 and remains at that level until layer 20, after which it declines slightly.

The “ffn_output” signal (green dash-dot line) exhibits periodic spikes at layers 5, 13, and 22, reaching peak values of approximately 800 at each of these points.

The “ffn_residual” signal (red solid line) rises sharply at layer 5 to approximately 1400 and remains at that level until layer 20, after which it declines slightly.
model_annotations.Chinese: This line chart, titled "Massive Activation of baseline," displays the maximum activation values across layers for four distinct signal components within a neural network under baseline conditions. The x-axis, labeled "Layer," is linear and spans from 0 to 20, with tick marks at regular intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "Max Activation Value," is linear and ranges from 0 to 1600, with tick marks at regular intervals of 200. The chart includes four lines: the "attn_output" is shown as a blue dashed line, the "attn_residual" as an orange dotted line, the "ffn_output" as a green dash-dot line, and the "ffn_residual" as a red solid line. The red solid line (ffn_residual) begins near zero, rises sharply to approximately 1400 at layer 5, and remains between 1400 and 1600 through layer 20 before declining to approximately 600 at layer 22. The orange dotted line (attn_residual) follows a similar trajectory, rising sharply to approximately 1400 at layer 5, maintaining values between 1400 and 1600 through layer 20, and declining to approximately 600 at layer 22, with its peak occurring at layer 22. The green dash-dot line (ffn_output) remains near zero until layer 5, then spikes to approximately 800 at layer 5, dips to near zero at layer 10, spikes again to approximately 800 at layer 13, dips to near zero at layer 15, and spikes once more to approximately 800 at layer 22. The blue dashed line (attn_output) remains near zero throughout all layers, with no notable increase at any point in the network.
